notes: Translated from OVAL's validation file constraint_instead_of_refinement, which OVAL's SHACL validator must reject. Kept: the first permission's action, target, and duty, whose compensate action carries the misplaced constraint. Dropped: the first permission's print refinement, assignee, and dateTime constraint; the second permission, which carries other defects (odrl:create and odrl:adminLevel are not ODRL terms; a refinement on a party collection as assignee, which due2 rejects as UnsupportedConstruct; a constraint on an example.com left operand; an untyped dateTime); the third permission, a plain compensate on the same target, which the placement test does not need; OVAL's example profile IRI. Changed: rules named; Rule and Constraint types added; conflict and profiles declared; the right operand 50, an xsd:integer, written as xsd:decimal with a unit IRI. The constraint's place is as authored. Written as odrl:refinement, it would be oval-duty-payment's pay-at-least idiom with eq. OVAL keeps no result beyond the rejection.

expected_rejection.why: The action node of the duty <http://example.com/policy:6161#pay> carries an odrl:constraint, and the ODRL vocabulary places a constraint only on a Policy or a Rule (Vocabulary §3.14.2); an action is narrowed by odrl:refinement (IM §2.5.4). Normalisation rejects a constraint outside its place in stage 1 (odrl-compound-to-atomic-normalization.md §3), so W1 rejects the policy.

oval_expected.result: invalid: OVAL's SHACL validator must reject it
